AccountCreateParams.description: How the UI creates an account.

removeWorkspace.description:
Whether the workspace directory goes too. Defaults to FALSE.

Explicit because deleting somebody's files as a side effect of removing their login is not a
decision a default should be making.

AccountSummary.description:
One account, as the control UI lists it.

The principal and its profile flattened into one row on purpose. Every consumer needs both, they
are stored apart only because identity and accounts are separate layers, and making the page do
the join means the page owns a rule about what happens when one half is missing.

advertisedTools.description:
The subset of `tools` whose DEFINITIONS are sent to the model.

A rendering choice, never a permission — the deferred-tool catalog uses it to keep a thousand
schemas out of the context window while leaving the tools reachable through `tool_call` and
through a name the model remembers. `tools` and `excludeTools` are what decide whether a call
runs; conflating the two is how "the model was not shown it" gets mistaken for "the model
cannot use it", which is only true of a model that is not being steered by anybody.

The agent's own system prompt, replacing the default persona entirely when set.

Per-agent rather than global because a deployment runs several agents with genuinely different
jobs — a code reviewer and a support responder should not share a persona.

The exact command or path, so an operator approves what will actually run.

Carried because an approval prompt without it is a rubber stamp: "run a shell command" is not

reasoningEffort.description: Per-turn reasoning preference; never changes the saved agent configuration.

targetTimeSeconds.description: Soft task time target in seconds; never a cancellation deadline.

userId.description: The principal the turn is billed and authorized as.

attachments.description: Delivered files; IDs match attachment events so clients can deduplicate.

sessionKey.description:
The session id this turn was filed under — `sessions.get`'s id, not the provider's.

The one field a client needs to mirror its own conversation. `conversationId` is null for
every provider that does not hold history itself, and even when it is not, the gateway's
session key is namespaced by principal: a client that subscribed to what it typed named
`main` while the record was `alice::main`, so `sessions.subscribe` refused it and the second
device watched nothing. Passing this straight back as the next turn's `conversationId`
resumes the same conversation, so a client never has to reconstruct the namespacing itself.

Absent from a gateway older than this field. Every reader here treats a missing value as
"this server cannot tell me" rather than declaring it optional, because it is never optional
on the server that produced it.

enforcement.description:
What happens at the cap.

`block` refuses further spend; `warn` records and allows it. The default is `warn`, because a
budget that silently halts an enterprise agent mid-task is a worse failure than an overrun
somebody can see — blocking must be chosen deliberately.

period.description: The window the cap applies over.

scopeId.description: The scope's id (a user id, an agent id…). Ignored for `global`.

ConfigResult.description: The effective configuration, with secrets removed.

defaults.description:
The configuration as it would be with no file and no environment at all.

Sent so a UI can offer a settings EDITOR rather than a settings viewer. Three things need it
and none can be derived from the merged config alone: the type of a key the operator has not
set yet (an absent key has no value to infer one from), whether the current value differs from
the shipped one, and what "reset" would restore. Without it a console can only show what is
set, which is precisely the half an operator already knows.

value.description:
The value, already parsed.

A JSON value rather than a string, unlike the CLI's argument: a caller speaking this protocol
has types, and re-parsing a string here would make `"true"` and `true` indistinguishable at
exactly the boundary where the difference matters.

nonce.description: The challenge nonce, proving the client read the server's first frame.

type.description:
The model's reasoning trace. `signature` is Anthropic's integrity token: it MUST be
round-tripped verbatim on a later turn or the API rejects the thinking block.
Reasoning the provider encrypted. Opaque, and round-tripped as-is.
An encoded video or animation container decoded natively by a multimodal model.
One ordered frame of a video or animation. Consecutive frames form one clip.

signature.description:
An integrity token some providers attach to a tool call made while reasoning.

Opaque, and round-tripped verbatim on the next turn. Gemini rejects a replayed function
call whose thought signature is missing or altered, so this must travel WITH the block
rather than in a side table — a cache keyed by call id does not survive a session being
reloaded from disk, which is exactly when the replay happens.

type.description:
The model asking for a tool to run. `id` is the provider's own call id and is what a
result must quote back.

inspectedMediaSha256.description: Host-authored observation evidence; never inferred from result prose.

DeviceApproveParams.description: Approving a device, optionally overriding the scopes it asked for.

scopes.description:
Absent grants exactly what the device requested. A list here REPLACES that, and may widen it.

Stated plainly because the previous wording ("may only NARROW it") was false of every
implementation: `MemoryPairingStore.approve` does `grant(..., scopes ?? requestedScopes)` and
never compares the two. Widening is the intended behaviour and not an oversight — a device
that sends no `x-nexa-scopes` header is recorded as requesting `read`, which is every client
that has not been told otherwise, so a narrow-only rule would make it impossible to pair your
own laptop as an admin without first re-pairing it with a hand-set header.

It is not a privilege escalation BY the device: `devices.approve` requires `admin`, so the
only party that can widen a grant is one that already holds everything it is granting.

DeviceApproveResult.description: What `devices.approve` hands back. The token is plaintext exactly once.

DeviceInfo.description: A paired device, without the credential.

DeviceListResult.description:
The device roster: what is paired and what is asking to be.

One method for both halves because they are one screen and one decision — an operator looking at
a pending request needs to see whether that device is already paired under another name, and two
round trips to find out is two chances for the two lists to be read from different moments.

DeviceRequestInfo.description: A device waiting for an operator, as it appears on the wire.

Flatten<{readonlytitle:string|null;reado.description:
Collapses the required/optional intersection into one object type.

Homomorphic (`in keyof T` over a naked type parameter), so `readonly` and `?` are carried through
rather than flattened away — without it every derived type would lose its modifiers and a caller
could assign to a field the store treats as immutable.

The scope each method requires.

Sent because the alternative is every client shipping its own copy of the server's
authorization table, which then drifts: a UI that greys out the wrong button is a support
ticket, and one that offers a button the server refuses is worse.

Job.description: A scheduled job as it is stored.

allowConcurrent.description:
Whether a new run may start while a previous one is still going.

Default false. An every-minute job whose run takes 90 seconds will otherwise pile up runs
until the process dies — the classic naive-scheduler failure.

enabled.description: Disabled jobs stay stored and stop firing.

graceMs.description: For {@link MisfirePolicy.RunIfRecent}: how stale a missed occurrence may be.

maxRetries.description: How many times a failed run is retried before the occurrence is abandoned.

owner.description: Who owns this job, for permissions and for credit attribution.

timeoutMs.description: A hard ceiling on one run, after which it is aborted and recorded as timed out.

deliverTo.description: Where the reply goes: a channel id, or absent to leave it in the session.

kind.description: Run an agent turn with this prompt. The ordinary case.

silentWhenEmpty.description: Suppress delivery when the turn produced nothing worth sending.

allowSelfLifecycle.description:
Allow a command that stops or restarts Nexa itself.

Refused by default because scheduling one from inside the scheduler is a loop rather
than a task — see `assertNotLifecycleCommand`. A nightly restart is a legitimate thing
to want, and this is how to say so.

elevation.description:
Run this command outside the sandbox, if the policy allows it.

The operator's own decision about their own machine, which is why it lives on a job
they wrote and not on an argument a model fills in. Authorized against the policy at
the moment of the spawn: `sandbox.required` refuses it outright, and anything stronger
than `sandbox.elevation` is refused as exceeding it.

A backup script that has to read outside the workspace roots is the case this exists
for — before it, the elevation axis was declared, defaulted to `off`, and unreachable.

kind.description: Run a shell command. Its stdout becomes the run's output.
Call a registered tool directly, with no model in the loop.
Emit an event other subsystems subscribe to.

Housekeeping: expired media, expired workspaces, memories past their TTL.

A kind rather than a `shell` job because the work is in-process — it needs the media
store, the workspace manager and the memory store this deployment constructed, not a
command line — and because a deployment should not have to write a cron entry to stop
accumulating every screenshot anybody ever sent it.

JobAction.description: What a job does when it fires.

JobAddParams.description:
A scheduled job, in the two shapes an operator actually creates.

Narrower than the scheduler's own `JobTrigger`/`JobAction` unions on purpose: the wire is a
public surface and every shape on it has to be validated, versioned and documented forever. A
scheduled prompt and a scheduled command are what a TUI or an IDE asks for; the full union stays
internal and reachable through the scheduler API.

cron.description: A cron expression. Exactly one of `cron`, `intervalMs` and `at` must be given.

deliverTo.description:
Where the answer goes, as `channel:conversation` — `telegram:12345`.

Absent leaves the answer in the run record, which is what a job that exists to do something
rather than to say something wants. A reminder wants the opposite.

prompt.description: An agent turn to run. Exactly one of `prompt` and `command` must be given.

silentWhenEmpty.description: Say nothing when the turn produced nothing. A quiet night should be quiet.

JobOwner.description: Who a job belongs to — the four scopes credit is tracked against.

expression.description: A five- or six-field cron expression, or an `@daily`-style alias.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone; occurrences are local wall-clock times in it.

kind.description: Every `intervalMs`, measured from the last completion.

ListSchema.description: A list is a finalized collection; it is not a stream.

LogTailParams.description: A window over the recent log.

level.description: Only lines at or above this level.

limit.description: How many lines back to read. Absent reads everything the buffer still holds.

scope.description: Only lines from this subsystem, e.g. `gateway`.

since.description: Only lines newer than this timestamp, so a poller does not re-read what it has.

MediaAcknowledgeParams.description: Client attachment handler outcome; receipt does not assert that a human viewed it.

MisfirePolicy.description:
What to do about occurrences that elapsed while the process was down.

There is no safe default here, which is exactly why it is a per-job field. A daily digest that
missed three days should send ONE digest (`run-once`); a billing rollup that missed three days
must process all three (`run-all`); a "remind me at 9am" whose 9am passed six hours ago should
probably stay quiet (`skip`). Choosing one globally is wrong for the other two.

identity.description: Durable host metadata; provider adapters send only the role and content to models.

item.description: The item this agent is working.

role.description: Its role on the team, when the engine names one. Empty otherwise.

`working` | `done` | `failed` | `retired`. Retired means it stood down and a fresh agent
takes the item on, which is not the same as the item failing.

tokens.description: Completion tokens this agent has spent, as the engine measured them.

Which turn this agent is on. There is NO `turnsAllowed` beside it: nothing bounds an agent's

arguments.description: Raw JSON arguments, exactly as the agent wrote them.

item.description: The backlog item whose agent is asking, for attribution in the UI.

NcapArtifactDelta.description:
One item's DELIVERABLE, as it closes — the counterpart to a finding for work that MAKES rather
than checks.

title.description: The item's own title. An artifact carries no location and no severity to anchor it.

NcapAsrTranscript.description: Native ASR result over exact mono 16 kHz input.

blockId.description: Server-assigned numeric id, stable across the block's begin/delta/end.

blockKind.description:
The block kind on `begin`: `code`, `bash`, `file_write`, `read`, `search`, `list`, `diff`,
or `ask`. The server classifies the model's fenced action vocabulary into these.

language.description: The language on a `begin` for a code block.

query.description: The query on a `begin` for a `search` block.

NcapDelta.description:
A single streamed delta from the engine.

Under NCAP the server DECODES the model stream into typed packets, so a delta carries exactly one
of: answer `content`, `reasoning`, an engine `status`, a `block` phase, a `tool` call, or one of
the out-of-band reports (graph, backlog, roster, findings, learning, research, skills).

agent.description: One agent's own record from the live fan-out, for the roster.

agentId.description:
The response's numeric `agent_id`. `0` for a plain turn; in a batch it is the sub-request's
`subId`, so the caller routes each delta to the right sub-stream.

agentTool.description: A sub-agent asking for a tool to be run on its behalf.

artifact.description: One item's DELIVERABLE, as that item closes.

asr.description: Native transcription, separate from assistant content.

acceptance.description: The criteria this item is judged against, in the planner's own words.

points.description: The planner's estimate. Drives a client's Definition-of-Ready model.

activity.description: What the agent said it is doing this turn, in its own words. Empty until it says.

turn.description:
Which turn this item's agent is on. `0` before it has taken one. There is no ceiling to
divide it by: nothing bounds an agent's turns.

stoppedBy.description: Why the run stopped, in words, so a PARTIAL run can say that it is partial.

backlog.description: A live backlog the ENGINE built for this turn: the goal decomposed and fanned out.

block.description: A live rich-block phase (begin/delta/end) decoded server-side.

content.description: Answer content for this chunk (empty on a non-content chunk).

conversationId.description: The server-owned conversation id for this turn, surfaced early (from `AgentBegin`).

expert.description: The EXPERT the server's pre-flight reflection chose to handle this turn.

finding.description: One DEDUPED finding from a closed fan-out, with its words.

geometry.description: Native 3D generation event; binary asset data stays outside model text.

graph.description: A live project-graph event for the knowledge-graph view.

preflight.description: The full pre-flight reflection for the panel shown before the answer streams.

reasoning.description: Reasoning / thinking-trace text for this chunk (empty on a non-reasoning chunk).

reflection.description:
The reflection stage's reasoning. Display-only: it never becomes part of the persisted
assistant turn.

research.description: One step of working an UNSOLVED problem.

status.description: An out-of-band engine lifecycle status carried by a chunk with no text.

steer.description: One SUPERVISION ROUND of a decomposed run.

tool.description: A tool call the client must execute.

usage.description: A live, non-terminal token-usage / progress update.

video.description: One accepted/progress/content/end event from native video generation.

voice.description: 80 ms of the model speaking, 24 kHz mono PCM16.

NcapFindingDelta.description: One deduped finding a decomposed run produced, as the engine holds it.

evidence.description: The worker's own supporting quote. Empty when it gave none.

location.description:
`path:line`, or whatever locator the worker gave. One string: the engine does not guarantee
the `path:line` shape, so splitting it would invent a line number.

reporters.description: EVERY item that reported it, not just the copy that survived the dedup.

seen.description: How many workers reported this same defect.

NcapGraphDelta.description:
A live project-graph event decoded from a `Graph*` frame. The server streams the codebase graph as
it builds it: `begin` opens a graph session (the client resets its store for it), `node`/`edge`
append entities/relations, `grounding` updates the active subgraph highlight, and `end` marks the
batch complete.

NcapGraphEdge.description: One relation decoded from a `GraphEdge` frame.

kind.description: An edge-kind string; exact kinds carry confidence 1, probabilistic ones below 1.

NcapGraphNode.description: One code entity decoded from a `GraphNode` frame.

kind.description: A node-kind string (e.g. `file`, `function`); the store validates it.

NcapGraphSpan.description: A source location decoded from a graph frame: where an entity or relation is evidenced.

NcapGrounding.description: The grounding overlay decoded from a `GroundingUpdate` frame (the active/highlighted subgraph).

NcapResearchDelta.description: One step of a research run on an unsolved problem.

claim.description: The claim in one line, when the frame carries one.

detail.description: The engine's own line for this frame.

disputed.description: True when ANOTHER line settled this same claim the OTHER way. Orthogonal to `status`.

line.description: The line of attack this frame is about, or empty when it is about the run itself.

lines.description: How many lines of attack are open.

phase.description:
`opened` | `working` | `reported` | `again` | `settled` | `bare`, or `unknown` from a newer
engine. `bare` means the run established nothing, which is an HONEST outcome of research and
must never be rendered as an error.

problem.description: The problem being worked, as the user stated it. Never empty.

roundsTotal.description: Rounds across EVERY run this machine has done on this problem.

status.description:
`failed` | `inconclusive` | `cases` | `reduced` | `refuted` | `proved`, or null before a line
has reported. Never collapse these: `reduced` is not a proof and `cases` is not a theorem.

tokens.description: What the run has cost so far, as the engine estimates it.

NcapSkillDelta.description: One skill the engine ingested, and what it has done this run.

always.description: Whether it bypasses matching and applies to every item.

applied.description: How many it was actually injected into. Lower than `matched` means the budget bit.

checkable.description:
Whether it carries a `requires:`/`forbids:` clause the engine can CHECK rather than only
inject — the difference between a directive that is enforced and one merely offered.

matched.description: How many items it matched this run.

source.description: `project` | `claude` | `user` — where it was found, which is also its precedence.

NcapSteerDelta.description: One supervision round of a decomposed run: what the supervisor concluded and every directive.

item.description: The item it names, or null for a directive that names none. Item id 0 is a REAL id.

summary.description: The supervisor's own statement of what was achieved, when it signed the goal off.

NcapToolCall.description: A tool the server asked the client to execute, decoded from the model stream.

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments (may be partial JSON while `partial` is true).

partial.description:
A live preview of a call the model is still typing: render the forming action but do NOT
execute it. The authoritative call (no `partial`) arrives at completion and is what runs.

NcapUsage.description: Live, non-terminal token usage for the whole turn.

cachedTokens.description: The subset of `promptTokens` served from the prefix cache.

ObjectSchema.description: Closed objects reject accidental fields, while open objects retain extension data.

OkResult.description: The answer to a method that only reports success.

PendingApproval.description: One approval waiting for a human.

detail.description:
The exact command or path, so an operator approves what will actually run.

Carried because an approval prompt without it is a rubber stamp: "run a shell command" is not
a decision anybody can make. It is the tool's own rendering, never the model's prose.

PerformanceCohort.description: Input capability reports are not hardware or operating-system identification.

PerformanceGroup.description: Aggregate metrics expose no player/session identifiers. Counts are decimal strings.

PerformanceQuery.description: End-exclusive server-observed report timestamps; sample windows can begin before fromMs.

PerformanceReport.description: Complete bounded selection with quality counts and collection diagnostics.

collection.description: Owner-visible collection evidence, not a guarantee that the game emitted every required event.

PersonalAgent.description: A user's own agent instructions; execution permissions always come from the deployment default.

PersonalAgentInput.description: Create with an empty id, or update an existing owned agent.

PlanningAlignmentAnchor.description: Server-created semantic anchors for the request and the proposed graph.

PlanningBrief.description: A bounded product brief; unanswered operational choices remain explicit.

PlanningDocument.description: Unsaved editor state is planning context, never an execution plan or permission grant.

PlanningReply.description: Fingerprint pins the proposal to unsaved state as well as the persisted base revision.

alignment.description: Omitted on older stored replies; never supplied by the model.

sourceIds.description: Explicit metadata selections; never resource grants. Omitted by older clients.

PlanningRequirement.description: Links the user's intent to stable component identities without claiming execution readiness.

PlanningRequirementFingerprint.description: A fingerprint detects graph drift; it never proves a requirement is fulfilled or runnable.

PlanningSource.description: Metadata only. No filesystem paths, credentials, file contents, or host telemetry.

PlanningSourceState.description: Discovery of a registered source is not a grant or an executable resource binding.

PlanningSourcesRequest.description: Owner-scoped catalog pagination; a cursor is an opaque source identity, not a path.

PlanningTurn.description: A turn is a separate bounded record, not an ever-growing workflow field.

sourceIds.description: Explicit metadata selections retained with this conversation turn.

ProcessInput.description: Keystrokes are bounded and addressed through the owning session.

ProcessLogRef.description: Incremental reads share the same bounded log endpoint as background job tails.

ProcessResize.description: Terminal dimensions are small positive integers.

effort.description:
How hard the model should think before answering.

Six tiers rather than four because the ends of the range are real and providers price them apart.
`Minimal` is a distinct setting on current OpenAI models — nearly no reasoning, but not none —
and `XHigh` is the recommended tier for agentic coding on several of them. A five-tier ladder
makes both unreachable, which means a caller cannot request the setting the provider itself
recommends. A provider without a given tier ladders DOWN to its nearest supported one.

include.description: Whether the reasoning trace should be streamed back at all.

maxTokens.description: A hard token budget for the reasoning trace, where the provider accepts one.

ReminderAction.description: A durable message to the conversation that requested it; no model execution.

ResetAllowanceParams.description: A confirmed reset always applies to the exact displayed allowance generation.

ResetAllowanceResult.description: A successful mutation carries its immutable receipt, including on retries.

ResetHistoryEntry.description: Owner-scoped reset evidence without operator grant/payment identifiers.

ResetSnapshot.description: JSON-safe reset state; generation tokens prevent stale tabs consuming another entitlement.

ResourceBinding.description: Saved requirement, including incomplete drafts. Never stores credentials or telemetry.

consumerId.description: Stable node/group identity controls which agent or step receives access.

maxAgeMs.description: Null allows unknown freshness. Otherwise runtime requires a fresh observed source time.

ResourceFamily.description:
External resource identity; these families never confer access themselves.
Supported external resource families, distinct from account tenancy.

ResourceLimits.description: Bounded read or job outputs, not a grant to ingest a whole source.

maxBytes.description: Unsigned canonical decimal, lossless on the JSON wire.

ResourceSchema.description: Resource roles are nominal identities, not implicit runtime permissions.

ResourceSelection.description: An exact dataset/endpoint selection; paths never act as implicit permission prefixes.

ResourceUse.description:
Attaching access, reading data, and placing computation are different operations.
Meaning of a resource binding in the graph.

ReverseApplicationSnapshot.description: Bounded projection for live Chat events; complete indexes are paged by the native query tool.

ReverseArchiveRef.description: A session-owned archive, without query tokens or analyzer handles.

ReverseCatalogPage.description: An append-only catalog page; cursors are exact decimal record offsets.

ReverseCatalogQuery.description: Reads only an authenticated session's indexed investigation, never a workspace path.

ReverseEvidencePage.description: Original evidence text paged by UTF-16 offset, independent of model report previews.

originalEvidenceSha256.description: Present for a derived code page and always identifies the unmodified captured original.

ReverseEvidenceQuery.description: Evidence ids come from the saved catalog and cannot authorize arbitrary files.

representation.description: Code is extracted at capture time; original remains the default.

ReverseEvidenceRecord.description: Provenance for one immutable evidence file, shared by specialists in the same run.

ReversePlanStep.description: An evidence-linked follow-up requested by a specialist and executed by the runtime.

ReverseRunSnapshot.description: Bounded, capability-free projection carried by live tool events and the final receipt.

application.description: Bounded projection for live Chat events; complete indexes are paged by the native query tool.

archive.description: A session-owned archive, without query tokens or analyzer handles.

kind.description: The runtime selects a target adapter; callers may make the choice explicit for ambiguous files.

ReverseState.description:
Runtime task lifecycle, distinct from the truth of model-authored findings.
Possible task and workflow states.

ReverseTaskSnapshot.description: A runtime-owned step in the shared investigation plan. Reports remain unverified findings.

RobloxCredentialStatus.description: Presence only: neither saved key material nor claims about Roblox permissions.

ScalarSchema.description: Primitive or named envelope type. Number values must be finite and safely represented.

SchemaField.description: Named nested field contracts keep missing, null and empty values distinct.

SessionFileParams.description: Identifies a saved file within an owned session.

SessionHistoryData.description: A small live notification; large records remain in bounded authenticated pages.

SessionHistoryPage.description: Bounded binary pages can split even a very large individual native event.

SessionHistoryParams.description: Byte cursors are decimal strings so large journals retain exact offsets.

pageBytes.description: Optional bounded read window, up to 1 MiB.

SessionHistoryRecord.description: Append-only presentation history, independent of model-context compaction.

SessionMessageData.description: The payload of a {@link GATEWAY_EVENTS.SessionMessage} event.

attachments.description: Attachments sent with this message, preserved for session viewers.

principalId.description: Who sent it, so a shared-agent transcript can attribute the turn to a person.

streamId.description: The run this message started, so a viewer can join the stream already in flight.

SessionRef.description: Names one session, for the subscription methods.

ShareMemberParams.description: Adds, re-modes or removes one subject. A `mode` of null removes.

ShareSummary.description: A shared folder, as the UI lists it.

SitePreview.description: Only server-fetched raster bytes cross the gateway; clients never fetch the visited host.

SourceLanguage.description: Source grammars are explicit; bytecode formats use separate version-aware adapters.

SteerParams.description: A correction for the server-minted active run, not a follow-up turn.

StreamAccepted.description: The acknowledgement of a streaming run.

inputId.description: Original saved input identity, assigned by the authorized gateway.

runId.description:
The SERVER's name for the run, which is the one `tasks.*` uses.

Distinct from `streamId` because the stream id is chosen by the client — deliberately, so the
accept response cannot race the first events — and two clients therefore pick the same one
routinely. A `tasks.cancel` keyed on the client's id would abort somebody else's run by
coincidence; keyed on this one it cannot.

sessionKey.description: Resolved durable conversation identity, including a newly allocated chat.

StreamParams.description: What one turn is asked for, when the client wants its events streamed.

attachments.description: User-authored image, video, document, and text blocks, in display order.

message.description: User text; may be blank when at least one attachment contains content.

reasoningEffort.description: Per-turn reasoning preference; never changes the saved agent configuration.

streamId.description:
The stream's id, chosen by the CLIENT.

Deliberate: the accept response and the first events can arrive in the same TCP segment, so a
client that waited for a server-assigned id would already have dropped events by the time it
had somewhere to put them. Letting the client name the stream removes the race entirely.

targetTimeSeconds.description: Soft task time target in seconds; never a cancellation deadline.

userId.description: The principal the turn is billed and authorized as.

TaskRecord.description:
One streaming run, as an operator or a second client sees it.

Reported from the gateway's own registry rather than from the agent, because the gateway is the
only place that knows which CONNECTION owns a run — and "cancel the run my phone started from my
laptop" is the reason this family exists at all.

connectionId.description: The connection that started it. Two clients of one principal are distinguishable.

runId.description:
The id `tasks.cancel` takes, and the reason this is not `streamId`.

A listing whose entries could not be acted on would be a screen with a Cancel button that has
nothing to send: the stream id is the CLIENT's name for the run, two clients pick the same one
routinely, and a cancel keyed on it would abort somebody else's turn by coincidence.

TeamMemberParams.description: Adds or removes one principal. `member: false` removes.

TeamSummary.description: A team, as the UI lists it.

TelemetryFunnelParams.description: Wire queries never carry an owner: the authenticated gateway supplies it.

TelemetryHealth.description: Owner-visible collection evidence, not a guarantee that the game emitted every required event.

TelemetryMonitorAction.description: Scheduler stores the rule; identity is only in Job.owner, never supplied by this action.

destination.description: Host-captured private channel destination; never accepted from model arguments.

TelemetryMonitorRule.description: A deterministic observed-conversion threshold, not an automatic causal experiment decision.

TelemetryNotificationDestination.description: Host-captured private channel destination; never accepted from model arguments.

TelemetryPerformanceParams.description: Complete bounded client performance query for one owned project.

TelemetryProject.description: Project identity returned to authenticated owners; contains no ingestion secret.

cacheWriteLongTokens.description:
Cache writes billed at a longer time-to-live, where the provider prices two tiers.

Separate from `cacheWriteTokens` because they are billed at different rates; folding them
together would misprice every request that uses the longer tier.

cacheWriteTokens.description: Input tokens written INTO the cache by this request, where the provider bills them apart.

cachedInputTokens.description: Input tokens served from a prompt cache (already counted in `inputTokens`).

contextTokens.description:
How much of the model's context window the conversation currently OCCUPIES.

Distinct from `inputTokens`, and the distinction is load-bearing for compaction. `inputTokens`
is a billing figure that accumulates across a turn's several round-trips; occupancy is the
size of the prompt right now. A compaction trigger that watched the billing figure would fire
early on every tool-heavy turn — after five round-trips the cumulative input exceeds the
window while the actual prompt is nowhere near it.

reasoningTokens.description: Reasoning tokens (already counted in `outputTokens` for most providers).

ToolCall.description: A tool call the model asked for.

ToolOutcome.description: One tool call's outcome, paired back to its call.

attachment.description: Transient visual progress for the active chat; never persisted in the transcript.

fraction.description: Completed fraction in `[0, 1]`, when the tool can know it.

reverse.description: Shared investigation plan and evidence provenance, without live query capabilities.

terminal.description: Live pseudoterminal identity for authenticated input and resize controls.

text.description: Text appended to the live view.

ToolProgressAttachment.description: A partial update from a running tool.

ToolQuestion.description: A question that may be rendered interactively by a conversation surface.

ToolQuestionChoice.description: One finite answer offered by a tool-originated question.

description.description: Optional detail used by menu-capable surfaces.

value.description: The inbound text produced by a press. Defaults to the label.

commandExecution.description: Only the execution adapter supplies this evidence; stdout cannot forge it.

content.description:
What the model sees. A string for the ordinary case; blocks when the result carries an image
or a document the model should actually look at.

continuation.description:
The exact call that would show the next page of this result, written by the tool.

Supplied by the TOOL and by nothing else, because only the tool knows its own argument names.
A shared builder would render `offset` for a tool whose parameter is `start_index`, and a
model handed a follow-up call that does not validate concludes paging is broken and gives up
on the rest of the output entirely. The registry copies it into the truncation marker when it
has to cut the result; a tool that pages itself puts it in `content` and leaves this unset.

deliveredMedia.description: Host receipt: true only after the attachment channel send resolves.

deliveredText.description: Text this tool already delivered to the user outside the agent's eventual reply.

deliveryReceipt.description: Exact submitted artifact and acknowledged destination, produced by the delivery adapter.

deliveryReceipts.description: One authoritative receipt per file in a multi-attachment delivery.

display.description:
Structured data for a UI that renders this tool specially (a diff view, a file tree).
Never sent to the model — that is what `content` is for.

inspectedMediaSha256.description: Original image digests successfully inspected by a vision route.

label.description: A short human label for a UI, e.g. `read 412 lines from src/main.ts`.

processMissing.description: The native process table confirmed the requested handle is absent for this session.

protocolPayload.description:
Preserve the string byte-for-byte instead of applying the registry's display-oriented
truncation. This is only for machine-readable protocol payloads whose consumer is the
provider itself, such as the paged project-graph manifest. Ordinary human/model output must
leave this unset and use `continuation` when it is large.

question.description:
A question handed back to the conversation surface for native delivery.

Finite choices become buttons or a menu on capable channels and numbered text elsewhere.
With no choices, the question remains an ordinary text reply. The channel router, not the
tool, owns delivery because only it knows the active address and platform capabilities.

reverse.description: Runtime-authored investigation receipt, retained in presentation history.

source.description: Where the content came from, for taint tracking.

terminate.description:
Whether this result should END the turn rather than feed back into the model.

Used by tools that hand control elsewhere (asking the user a question, yielding to another
agent). AND-ed across a batch, never OR-ed: one tool wanting to stop must not cancel the
results the model still needs from the others in the same batch.

truncation.description:
What the registry's backstop removed, when it removed anything.

Set on the way OUT, never by the tool. It exists because the marker in `content` is prose for
the model and a UI cannot parse prose: without this, a transcript view has no way to render
"this result was cut" as anything but a wall of text, and no way to offer the spill file as a
link. `undefined` means the result was returned whole.

It is PLUMBING, not a delivered feature: no UI in this repo reads it. It rides out to
embedders on `toolOutcomes`, which is a legitimate public API, but the transcript view that
would render a cut is not built and neither is the spill link — see `tools/output/Spill.ts`,
whose store the composition root does not construct.

verifiedCodePaths.description: Absolute source paths accepted by a native engineering workflow, never model-supplied.

ToolSitesData.description: Asynchronous tool decoration; may arrive after turn.end and never blocks it.

historyAt.description: Original event time, retained across checkpoint and replay.

historyId.description: Stable record identity shared by the immediate event and its later durable copy.

ToolStatus.description: What a tool did, from the agent's point of view.

ToolTerminal.description: A terminal belongs to the session that launched this exact process.

TruncationRecord.description: What a truncation did, in numbers the marker quotes and a UI can render.

continuation.description:
The exact call the model should make to see more, pre-rendered by the ORIGINATING tool.

Built by the tool because only the tool knows its own argument names; a shared builder would
guess `offset` for a tool that calls it `start` and hand the model a call that fails.

lastLinePartial.description:
Whether a cut fell mid-line, so one of the shown lines is a fragment.

`read` propagates this so `edit` never anchors a replacement on a fragment — an anchor that
matches half a line matches the wrong place in the file. For `tail` the fragment is the first
shown line rather than the last; it is one flag because one flag is all a consumer acts on.

shownChars.description:
Characters of the ORIGINAL text that survive, excluding anything this module synthesized.
Counted literally rather than script-weighted: a marker whose numbers disagree with what the
model can count for itself teaches it to distrust the whole marker.

spillPath.description: Where the complete content was written, when a spill store wrote it.

TruncationStrategy.description: How the content is reduced. Declared by the tool, which knows what it produced.

TurnEndData.description: The payload of a {@link GATEWAY_EVENTS.TurnEnd} event.

error.description: An error, in the shape a client can act on without parsing prose.

historyAt.description: Original event time, retained across checkpoint and replay.

historyId.description: Stable record identity shared by the immediate event and its later durable copy.

historyAt.description: Original event time, retained across checkpoint and replay.

historyId.description: Stable record identity shared by the immediate event and its later durable copy.

ValueSchema.description: Declarative portable schema subset. No callbacks, JavaScript evaluation, or credentials.

pcm.description: Base64 PCM16, mono, at the rate the call reported.

VoiceInterimEvent.description: Replaceable ASR hypothesis for the current utterance.

VoiceStartParams.description: Opens a spoken call. The conversation is the agent's, so a call can continue a typed thread.

frameBytes.description: One frame, in bytes. A client that sends a different size adds latency for nothing.

sampleRate.description: The rate to capture at and to play back at. Resampling anywhere else is a defect.

WalletHistoryEntry.description: A durable payment or settled request, without exposing provider payment identifiers.

WalletHistoryPage.description: Cursor pagination remains stable when new transactions arrive.

WalletSnapshot.description: Exact USD microcent balances encoded as decimal strings for JSON clients.

WireError.description: An error, in the shape a client can act on without parsing prose.

retryable.description: Whether repeating the SAME request could plausibly succeed.

WireTurnEvent.description:
A turn event as it travels.

Identical to {@link TurnEvent} except for the error variant: `Error` does not survive
`JSON.stringify` — it serializes to `{}` — so a failing turn would arrive as an empty object and
a client would report "something went wrong" with nothing else, forever.

WorkerState.description: Lifecycle states for Nexa's delegated workers.

WorkerStatus.description: One worker, identified independently of its shared persona. Times are decimal epoch milliseconds.

WorkflowCatalog.description: Catalog format is separate from saved component versions and draft storage format.

WorkflowCatalogObservation.description: An observation time is not a release date, freshness guarantee, or permission grant.

WorkflowCreateRequest.description: Client-chosen identities make an unacknowledged create safe to retry.

WorkflowDetails.description: User-owned descriptive fields, independent of run and automation state.

WorkflowEdge.description: A draft can retain a dangling edge so validation can explain an unfinished edit.

WorkflowEdgeKind.description:
Execution, values, and resource attachments have separate connection semantics.
Connection purpose does not depend on visual position.

WorkflowEndpoint.description: Stable endpoint identities survive cosmetic renames.

WorkflowGroup.description: Saved hierarchy owns parent-local geometry; collapse and viewport remain editor preferences.

WorkflowGroupPort.description: Published ports retain the original executable endpoint and explicit direction.

WorkflowGroupReference.description: Each revision references an immutable group body independently from executable node content.

WorkflowImageCandidate.description: All connected render quotes share the selected snapshot and its evidence.

WorkflowImageCapabilities.description: Supported image settings from the same adapter used by execution.

WorkflowImageDimensions.description: Pixel limits for a model that supports custom dimensions.

WorkflowImagePolicy.description: Image policies bound each complete render; token rate ceilings do not apply to image tariffs.

maxGenerationMicrocents.description: Null retains the existing run budget. A value additionally caps each image operation.

WorkflowImagePolicyEvidence.description: Immutable evidence for a concrete image model selected at run creation.

WorkflowImageQuote.description: An estimate creates no reservation and is recalculated when accepting a run.

WorkflowImageQuoteRequest.description: Unsaved render settings may be priced only in an owned workflow.

WorkflowImageRequirement.description: Per-operation settings sharing one reusable image-model binding.

WorkflowImageResolution.description: An unresolved policy has a reason, never an invented candidate or zero-price placeholder.

WorkflowImageResolutionRequest.description: A read-only policy preview uses unsaved settings and authenticated account pricing.

WorkflowImageSettings.description: An exact request, bounded before admission and independent of a text model binding.

operation.description: Older generation-only snapshots omit this field.

WorkflowListCursor.description: Cursor uses a timestamp plus stable identity to handle equal update times.

WorkflowListRequest.description: Metadata pagination carries no node payloads.

WorkflowManifestPage.description: Bounded manifest page; offsets count references, never bytes or revisions.

WorkflowModelCapability.description: Operations available through the workflow model picker.

WorkflowModelChoice.description: Public model metadata only: no endpoints, keys, account names, or adapter options.

availableAtCheck.description: Null/absent means no explicit endpoint check, rather than proof that a model is absent.

image.description: Present only for generation models; token prices do not describe image tariffs.

WorkflowModelFeature.description: Features that integrations can explicitly verify for model selection.

WorkflowModelPolicy.description: Saved, explicit constraints for the latest supported model on one provider.

maxCatalogAgeMs.description: Endpoint observation age, between one second and one day.

maxInputUsdPerMillion.description: Decimal USD per million tokens. Null is no additional rate ceiling.

WorkflowModelPolicyEvidence.description: The facts and constraints used for one immutable latest-policy decision.

WorkflowModelPrice.description: Existing ledger rate-card values, represented as decimal text without client-side money math.

WorkflowModelResolutionRequest.description: Owner-authorized policy preview; never saves a draft or performs inference.

WorkflowModelsPage.description: Registered providers and a bounded page from the selected provider's maintained catalog.

freshness.description: Legacy marker retained for older clients; endpoint check times are in observation.

observation.description: Optional for older clients. The legacy freshness marker remains unchanged.

WorkflowModelsRequest.description: Discovery never changes a workflow or grants access to another account's resources.

WorkflowNode.description: Versioned component configuration; unsupported or incomplete components can be saved.

WorkflowNodeReference.description: One node's immutable content and independently versioned layout.

WorkflowObject.description: JSON configuration is data, not an executable plan or authorization.

WorkflowPatch.description: A bounded edit; layout changes never include node configuration.

groups.description: Present together on hierarchy-aware edits; omission denotes a legacy writer.

WorkflowPosition.description: Personal viewport is excluded; these positions belong to the workflow itself.

WorkflowReadRequest.description: Null resolves the current revision only for the first page. Subsequent pages pin it.

WorkflowReceipt.description: Result retained by command receipts, including after subsequent edits.

WorkflowRecordPage.description: JSON text chunks are concatenated before parsing. Offsets count UTF-16 code units.

WorkflowRecordRequest.description: A reference identifies immutable content within the authenticated owner's workflow.

WorkflowRunArtifact.description: Public immutable file metadata; neither storage paths nor global media IDs cross this boundary.

WorkflowRunArtifactPage.description: A bounded binary fragment; clients verify the complete SHA-256 after assembling all fragments.

WorkflowRunArtifactRequest.description: One exact operation's artifact, addressed within the authenticated account and run.

WorkflowRunEventsRequest.description: Reads ordered journal events after an exclusive sequence.

WorkflowRunListPage.description: A bounded history page ordered by creation time and run ID.

WorkflowRunListRequest.description: Pages run history for one owned workflow.

WorkflowRunOutputPage.description: A bounded JSON fragment with total length and continuation offset.

WorkflowRunOutputRequest.description: Addresses one exact attempt and a UTF-16 offset into its encoded result.

WorkflowRunRequest.description: Addresses a run within the authenticated principal.

WorkflowRunStartRequest.description: Starts one idempotent run of an owned saved revision.

WorkflowRunStepsPage.description: A bounded step page and its continuation cursor.

WorkflowRunStepsRequest.description: Reads bounded step metadata after an exclusive node ID.

WorkflowSaveRequest.description: Command identity and expected revision serve different purposes.

WorkflowStepView.description: Exposes step metadata without embedding potentially large result payloads.

WorkflowSummary.description: Small management projection; contains no graph, prompts, or run histories.

WorkflowValidateRequest.description: Authoritative validation always names one immutable saved revision.

WorkflowValue.description: Large integers and financial values must use decimal strings.

Workspace.description: An isolated place an agent works.

destroyedAt.description: When the tree was removed. Present exactly on a tombstone.

expiresAt.description: When an ephemeral workspace should be reaped.

extraRoots.description: Additional roots tools may also reach (a shared cache, a read-only reference checkout).

leases.description: Runs currently holding it. Read through {@link activeLeases}, which drops expired ones.

owner.description: Who may use it. Absent means the deployment's default policy decides.

quota.description: Ceilings for this workspace's contents. Absent means unbounded — see {@link WorkspaceQuota}.

root.description: The absolute root. Every tool bound to this workspace is confined here.

state.description:
Where it is in its lifecycle.

Optional because records written before the lifecycle existed do not carry it, and those
records are on disk in every install that already made a workspace. Read it through
{@link stateOf}, which supplies the only truthful default for such a record: it was created
and it was never being destroyed, because the old destroy path deleted the row outright.

usage.description: Last known contents. Read through {@link usageOf}, which defaults a legacy record to zero.

worktree.description:
Set when this workspace IS a git worktree, so destroy unregisters it rather than deleting it.

Recorded on the workspace because destroy has to know: removing the directory of a worktree
leaves its registration in the source repository's `.git/worktrees`, and the branch stays
checked-out-somewhere forever with the name unusable.

WorkspaceCreateParams.description: What `workspaces.create` is asked for. Narrower than `CreateWorkspaceInput` — see the handler.

WorkspaceDescription.description: A workspace plus the lifecycle facts a caller has to see to make a decision about it.

destroyedAt.description: When the tree was removed. Present exactly on a tombstone.

expiresAt.description: When an ephemeral workspace should be reaped.

extraRoots.description: Additional roots tools may also reach (a shared cache, a read-only reference checkout).

leases.description: Only the leases still counting; expired ones are not shown because they hold nothing.

owner.description: Who may use it. Absent means the deployment's default policy decides.

quota.description: Ceilings for this workspace's contents. Absent means unbounded — see {@link WorkspaceQuota}.

root.description: The absolute root. Every tool bound to this workspace is confined here.

state.description:
Where it is in its lifecycle.

Optional because records written before the lifecycle existed do not carry it, and those
records are on disk in every install that already made a workspace. Read it through
{@link stateOf}, which supplies the only truthful default for such a record: it was created
and it was never being destroyed, because the old destroy path deleted the row outright.

usage.description: Last known contents. Read through {@link usageOf}, which defaults a legacy record to zero.

worktree.description:
Set when this workspace IS a git worktree, so destroy unregisters it rather than deleting it.

Recorded on the workspace because destroy has to know: removing the directory of a worktree
leaves its registration in the source repository's `.git/worktrees`, and the branch stays
checked-out-somewhere forever with the name unusable.

force.description: Overrides live leases. Recorded in the audit trail with the runs it overrode.

WorkspaceKind.description: How a workspace came to exist, which decides how it is cleaned up.

WorkspaceLeaseRecord.description:
One run's claim on a workspace, as stored in the record.

Durable rather than in-process, because the process holding the lease and the process asked to
destroy the workspace are routinely different ones — a gateway serving a conversation and a CLI
running `nexa workspace destroy`. An in-memory lease would be invisible to exactly the caller it
has to stop. `expiresAt` is what keeps a crashed run from pinning a workspace forever: a lease
nobody heartbeats stops counting on its own.

WorkspaceQuota.description:
The ceilings a workspace's contents may not pass.

Both are OPTIONAL and both default to absent, which means unbounded. That is deliberate and it is
the opposite of what the plan's "2 GiB by default" says: a user who tells the agent to clone a
10 GB monorepo into a workspace has asked for exactly that, and a default ceiling would refuse
the user's own instruction with an error about a limit they never chose. A quota here is a
runaway guard an operator sets on a shared deployment, or a bound a caller puts on one specific
workspace — never a product limit that arrives by omission.

maxBytes.description: Byte ceiling for the tree. Absent means unbounded.

maxFiles.description: File-count ceiling. Absent means unbounded — a million tiny files is invisible to a byte quota.

WorkspaceState.description:
Where a workspace is in its life.

The states exist because destruction is not instantaneous and must not be silent. A workspace
holds the user's work, so "delete it" has to pass through a phase where a run that is still
writing can stop it (`draining`), and a phase that survives a crash so the next start can finish
the job instead of finding a half-emptied tree behind a record that still says `active`
(`destroying`). `expired` is the grace state: a user who comes back a week after a task
workspace's TTL sees "this expired, here is how to keep it" rather than a vanished directory.

WorkspaceUsage.description: What a workspace currently holds, and when that was last measured against the disk.

reconciledAt.description:
When a full walk last corrected these numbers. `0` means never — the counters are then a
lower bound built from writes this process saw, which is honest but not authoritative.

description: All protocol contracts reachable from the public transport.
